newsitem.title: FINLAND: SILJA TRANSFERS FERRY TO SWEDISH REGISTER.
newsitem.headline: SILJA TRANSFERS FERRY TO SWEDISH REGISTER.

text.p: Passenger ferry operator Silja Oy will transfer to its Swedish subsidiary Silja Line Ab the Silja Festival ferry, and enter the vessel in Sweden's ship register, the transport ministry said in a statement received on Thursday.
Silja Festival will replace Silja Scandinavia on the Turku-Stockholm route in April 1997.

Silja's biggest competitor in passenger ferry traffic between Finland and Sweden, Viking Line AB, announced on November 18 it had purchased Silja Scandinavia from the Swedish company which had been leasing it to Silja.

The government justified its approval of Silja's application to transfer Silja Festival to the Swedish ship register by forecasting improved marketing prospects for Silja in Sweden thanks to the ferry flying the Swedish flag, instead of Finland's.
From April, five Silja Line ferries between Finland and Sweden will fly the Finnish flag and three vessels the Swedish one.
"The transfer of the vessel ... will strengthen Silja Line's operating conditions, particularly on the Swedish markets," the government said.
Part of Silja Scandinavia's crew will have the possibility to move to Silja Festival, but around 150 would be dismissed.
